events.title: Battle of Actium
events.description: Octavian's fleet, commanded by Marcus Agrippa, defeated the combined navies of Mark Antony and Cleopatra off the western coast of Greece. Antony and Cleopatra fled to Egypt with part of their fleet.
events.significance: The victory left Octavian the undisputed master of the Roman world. Within a few years he became Augustus, the first Roman emperor, and the Republic gave way to the Empire.

events.title: The Great Fire of London Begins
events.description: A fire broke out before dawn in a baker's shop on Pudding Lane. Strong winds spread it quickly through the crowded wooden streets, and it burned for four days.
events.significance: The fire destroyed the homes of most of the city's inhabitants, along with much of the medieval city. It led to rebuilding in brick and stone and to new fire-safety rules, and it gave Christopher Wren the chance to design a new St Paul's Cathedral.

events.title: U.S. Department of the Treasury Established
events.description: Congress created the Department of the Treasury, one of the first executive departments of the new federal government. Alexander Hamilton became its first Secretary.
events.significance: Hamilton used the department to put the young nation's finances on firm footing. His work shaped the country's banking, debt and fiscal systems.

events.title: Japan Formally Surrenders, Ending World War II
events.description: Japanese officials signed the instrument of surrender aboard the battleship USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay. General Douglas MacArthur accepted it on behalf of the Allied powers.
events.significance: The ceremony formally ended the Second World War, the deadliest conflict in human history, and began the Allied occupation of Japan.

events.title: Vietnam's Declaration of Independence
events.description: In Hanoi's Ba Dinh Square, Ho Chi Minh proclaimed the independence of Vietnam and the founding of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam.
events.significance: The declaration launched a new state and set off decades of struggle over its future. September 2 is still celebrated as Vietnam's National Day.
